{"body":"Decision first: I keep the account's concrete machinery but demote its guiding hypothesis to one among co-equal rivals; I accept the objection's three-way split and its attack on the recurrence test; I adopt the rival's second axis and, especially, its discriminating observation about reactions to proposals; I reject exactly one substantive move — the rival's opening conversation about what the flat is — and re-sequence accordingly.

What to use, with grounds. From the objection: the reported pattern is compatible with at least three readings — the words were genuinely unclear (ambiguity), the words were clear but circumstances changed and the dispute is whether the terms still bind (renegotiation), or the dispute is about who may raise and enforce the matter at all (legitimacy). I accept this split because it is cheap and tractable: inside a live dispute the three readings sound different. Semantic disputes cite what was said; renegotiation disputes cite what changed; legitimacy disputes cite who is talking. The objection's own problem record says the material cannot tell these apart — true of the written material, but the person asking is inside the disputes, not limited to the transcript. That converts the objection's gap into an instrument.

I also accept the objection's attack on the account's test: falling recurrence on specified items is consistent with every hypothesis in play, so it confirms none. One partial rehabilitation of the account, though: its third column — what happens when someone cannot do it — is already a standing renegotiation clause, so the specification probe quietly covers two of the three readings. That does not rescue the test's confirmatory claims; it means the probe is worth running even after granting the objection.

From the rival: the unit-versus-privacy axis is the one thing none of the three readings captures, and the rival's best contribution is not the axis but its instrument — when specifications are proposed, watch whether the avoiding flatmate engages with their content or pulls back from the proposal itself. Content-engagement supports the ambiguity or renegotiation readings; pullback from the very idea of a settled arrangement supports the rival's reading. That observation is cheap, runs during any probe, and actually discriminates where the recurrence count does not. I promote it to the primary instrument. I also promote the rival's truce-shaped arrangements — owned zones, default outcomes, no in-moment audit — from fallback to hedge, on grounds the rival itself did not give: removing the audit relation dissolves the standing question as well as the obligation question, so those arrangements fit the legitimacy reading as well as the privacy reading. It is the only proposed remedy that addresses two hypotheses at once. And the rival's own caution travels with it: any remedy carried by one side can be experienced by the other as an unreasonable demand, which matters because the asker is a party, not a manager standing above the dispute.

What to revise. The ordering. The objection is right that the account's most distinctive observation — the avoidance is likely about the form of the conversations — should go first. So the first move is one-to-one, with the smallest possible ask, about the conversations themselves rather than about any chore: not 'what is this flat' and not 'let's fix the bins', but roughly — these talks have become something you step away from; I would rather know what makes them bad than restart one. If the friend names the form (tone, scorekeeping, meetings that feel like tribunals), then chore specification is premature under every hypothesis, and the fix is conversational: a written channel, one item per exchange, no tallying. If the friend engages on content, proceed to the probe.

The probe itself: two or three genuinely recurring items, specified for done-ness, timing, and fallback — but co-drafted, not delivered. A note produced by two flatmates and handed to the third is a coalition document in a household that already has a withdrawal problem; the drafting is part of the test. While it runs, watch three signals instead of one: engagement with content versus pullback from the proposal; complaints ceasing versus migrating to new items or resurfacing at the next schedule change (migration and recurrence-after-change are what the rival hypotheses predict); and, within disputes that continue, whether they cite what was said, what changed, or who is speaking. None of this requires anyone to agree on a theory.

The threshold. The account's step 5 and the rival's r11 converge; I keep both with one tightening. The living-arrangement question should be named when even a no-audit truce arrangement is declined without any content engagement — earlier than indefinite deferral, later than a single failed chore talk. I will not set a number of attempts from this distance; it should be decided deliberately rather than by drift.

What to reject. The rival's opening move: asking each flatmate separately what they take the flat to be. For precisely the person who is withdrawing, that is a more demanding conversation than any chore talk — abstract, high-stakes, conducted with someone they are currently avoiding — so it repeats, at a higher level, the form problem the rival diagnoses. Detect the axis behaviorally through reactions to concrete proposals; ask directly only if engagement resumes. The axis stays; the opener goes.

One correction in the opposite direction: the objection overstates slightly when it says the thin material licensed an ordered plan — the account hedged throughout, as the objection's own self-objection half-concedes. The fair residue concerns emphasis and sequencing, absorbed above. I note it because taking the objection up wholesale would misdescribe the account it criticizes.

What stays open. Which of the now four hypotheses holds; whether the avoiding friend is acting in good faith — nothing here licenses a verdict either way; what the chores are, how long this has run, and what the friend has already said. The probe is designed so those answers arrive as byproducts rather than prerequisites. And the hard branch: if the friend will not engage even with the smallest ask about the conversations themselves, no chore-level probe can run, and the living-arrangement question arrives early, carried by silence rather than by evidence. That branch should be faced without being treated as a verdict on anyone.","commitments":"{"language":"FCL-1","records":[{"id":"n-cl1","type":"claim","text":"The three readings the objection separates — ambiguity of wording, renegotiation under changed circumstances, legitimacy of enforcement — are distinguishable from inside a live dispute: semantic disputes cite what was said, renegotiation disputes cite what changed, legitimacy disputes cite who is speaking.","grounds":"The objection states the distinction but treats it as undecidable from the material; the asker participates in the disputes and can hear these surface features in real time, so the distinction is usable even though the transcript cannot settle it.","mentions":["daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/objection#o1","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/objection#p1"]},{"id":"n-cl2","type":"claim","text":"The account's specification probe bundles two tests, not one: the done-ness and timing columns probe ambiguity, while the fallback column is a standing renegotiation clause and probes the renegotiation reading. It still says nothing about legitimacy or about the rival's unit-versus-privacy axis.","consequence":"Running the probe is worthwhile even granting the objection's critique, but its recurrence count confirms no hypothesis.","target":["daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/account#c2"],"mentions":["daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/objection#o2"]},{"id":"n-cl3","type":"claim","text":"Watching the reaction to a specification proposal — engagement with its content versus pullback from the proposal itself — discriminates the unit-versus-privacy reading from the ambiguity and renegotiation readings, which recurrence counting cannot do.","grounds":"Adopted from the rival as the primary instrument because it is cheap, runs during any probe, and addresses the discriminating-power gap the objection exposed in the account's test.","depends":["daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/rival#r7"],"mentions":["daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/objection#o2"]},{"id":"n-cl4","type":"claim","text":"Truce-shaped arrangements (owned zones, default outcomes, no in-moment audit) address the legitimacy reading as well as the privacy reading, because removing the audit relation dissolves the question of standing along with the question of obligation.","consequence":"Raises such arrangements from a fallback conditional on the rival's reading to a hedge offered before the living-arrangement question, without first requiring anyone to agree on what kind of household this is.","depends":["daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/rival#r8","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/objection#o1"]},{"id":"n-o1","type":"objection","text":"Asking each flatmate what they take the flat to be is, for the withdrawing flatmate, a more demanding conversation than any chore talk, and would likely be avoided for the same reasons the chore talks are avoided.","target":["daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/rival#r6"],"bearing":"If this holds, the unit-versus-privacy axis should be detected behaviorally through reactions to concrete proposals — and asked directly only if engagement resumes — rather than probed through a new abstract opening conversation; the rival's axis is preserved while its opener is dropped."},{"id":"n-o2","type":"objection","text":"The objection overstates when it says the account's thin material licensed an ordered sequence; the account hedged throughout, as the objection's own self-objection half-concedes.","target":["daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/objection#o3"],"mentions":["daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/objection#o4"],"bearing":"Limits the objection's uptake: its resequencing demand stands, its characterization of the account's assertiveness does not, and absorbing both wholesale would misdescribe the account."},{"id":"n-c1","type":"commitment","text":"Approach the avoiding flatmate one-to-one with the smallest possible ask about the conversations themselves, before any group discussion or drafted note.","scope":"The asker's next one or two attempts.","action":"Ask, in effect, what makes these talks worth stepping away from; do not open with a chore item or with the question of what the flat is.","consequence":"If the friend names the conversational form, change the form (written channel, one item per exchange, no tallying) before any specification work; if the friend engages on content, proceed to the probe in n-c2.","depends":["n-o1","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/objection#c1"],"revises":["daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/account#c3"]},{"id":"n-c2","type":"commitment","text":"Run the specification probe co-drafted, with the avoiding flatmate invited to co-author the two or three items, and treat falling recurrence as confirming nothing on its own.","scope":"Two or three genuinely recurring chores over the following weeks.","action":"Invite co-drafting rather than presenting a finished note; while the probe runs, observe three signals: engagement-with-content versus pullback-from-proposal, cessation versus migration or recurrence-after-schedule-change, and which of the three readings continuing disputes cite.","consequence":"Turns the account's single-signal test into a discriminating probe and prevents the clarification move from becoming a two-against-one coalition document.","depends":["n-cl1","n-cl2","n-cl3","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/objection#u1","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/rival#r9"],"revises":["daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/account#c2"]},{"id":"n-c3","type":"commitment","text":"If specification proposals draw pullback rather than content engagement, offer a no-audit truce arrangement; if that too is declined without any content engagement, name the living-arrangement question explicitly.","scope":"Contingent branches of the probe.","action":"Offer owned zones with default outcomes and no in-moment auditing; on failure, raise the lease-and-living-arrangement question rather than deferring it indefinitely or forcing it from a single chore dispute.","consequence":"Sequences remedies so that each step tests a different hypothesis and the larger decision arrives on evidence of repeated non-engagement rather than on drift.","depends":["n-cl3","n-cl4","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/rival#r8","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/rival#r11"]},{"id":"n-u1","type":"use","text":"Take up the objection's instruction to build the probe so that it tells rival hypotheses apart, the rival's reaction-to-proposal observation, and the account's smallest-recurring-cases mechanism, while setting aside the rival's opening question and the account's confirmatory reading of falling recurrence.","action":"Read n-c1 through n-c3 as the operative sequence and the four hypotheses as co-equal until the probe's signals separate them.","target":["daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/objection#u1","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/rival#r7","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/account#c2"]},{"id":"n-p1","type":"problem","text":"If the avoiding flatmate will not engage even with the smallest ask about the conversations themselves, no chore-level probe can run; the living-arrangement question then arrives early, carried by silence rather than by evidence, and neither the account, the objection, nor the rival supplies an instrument for that branch.","mentions":["n-c1"]},{"id":"n-p2","type":"problem","text":"What the chores are, how long the pattern has run, and what the avoiding flatmate has already said remain unknown; the probe is designed so these arrive as byproducts, but a long or lease-bound history could compress the sequencing in ways the material cannot determine. How many failed attempts justify raising the living-arrangement question likewise cannot be fixed from here and must be set deliberately rather than by drift.","mentions":["daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/account#p1","n-c3"]}],"uptake":["n-cl1","n-cl2","n-cl3","n-cl4","n-o1","n-o2","n-c1","n-c2","n-c3","n-u1","n-p1","n-p2"]}"}

Work on the problem using the material actually exposed in this request and your background knowledge. The problem has no supplied answer key or scoring rule. Claims, criticisms and methods are fallible. Do not invent a source, an observation, an earlier event, or a dependency to fill a field. A missing view says what you can currently see; it does not establish what happened earlier. Return a JSON object with exactly two independently authored string fields: body and commitments. Body is your public prose contribution. Commitments says what taking your contribution up would involve. An empty commitment surface is allowed when none can be identified. Do not repeat the body wholesale into commitments.

Use FCL-1 for the commitment surface, encoded as a JSON document inside the commitments string: {"language":"FCL-1","records":[...],"uptake":[...]}. Each record has unique local id, type (claim|commitment|objection|use|problem), and text (unrestricted prose). Optional prose fields: scope, action, consequence, grounds, bearing. Optional arrays of references: target, depends, mentions, revises, withdraws. References are local IDs or exposed-artifact-label#local-ID; do not invent hidden IDs. A commitment proposes a scoped use, action, application or consequence; an objection alleges a defect whose bearing can itself be criticized; a use proposes an uptake or response; a problem states an unresolved question. depends asserts reliance; mentions only locates material. uptake lists the records you currently propose to use, not certified truths. No record type or optional field must be present. Empty records and uptake are allowed. Express uncertainty or an unrepresentable relation in prose rather than inventing a relation. The body remains unrestricted prose.

Return one JSON object with exactly two string fields: "body" and "commitments". Write the actual commitments separately; do not copy the body into that field as a storage shortcut.

## Node response

Continue the inquiry in light of the account, criticism and alternative. Decide what to use, leave open, revise or reject, and explain your grounds where they matter.

## Original problem

I share a flat with two friends. We keep arguing about ordinary household chores. Sometimes we agree on who will do something, but later we disagree about what the agreement meant. Our work schedules change, and one friend has started avoiding the conversations. What should I do?

## Selected input account

Source account: daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/account; selected view: both
Artifact: cd6e3e2f307e0dac79543de9bed087db4ee7dcd40b3d989d3c6d4b02057d8b99
Original body SHA256: 360ee14fa7545c90cadf79c7d2fe9c157faf470d6368504b06768e36e0d13c79
Original commitments SHA256: bd7faa10242d5841c8063c7a0919a20706c658c4a2054a5729caeacbc3cd04c8
Delivery: COMPLETE; envelope: AUTHORED
BODY
The problem as posed is practical, and the material is thin: three flatmates, recurring disputes about ordinary chores, agreements that later turn out to have been understood differently, changing work schedules, and one friend withdrawing from the conversation. There is also a first-fork note saying the prior source was absent in the first template invocation, so there is no earlier account to inherit or revise against. I should not pretend to know what was said in prior conversations, what the chores are, who is avoiding whom, or why.

The most useful thing to conjecture is that the repeated disagreement is not primarily about willingness. Two people can agree that the dishes should be done and still disagree later about whether the agreement meant "by tonight," "before the kitchen is used again," or "on your turn." That is an ambiguity problem, not a motivation problem. Changing schedules make any fixed arrangement fragile, and avoidance is a predictable response when each conversation feels like relitigating fault. So the working hypothesis is: the household is running on spoken agreements with unstated specifications, and the cost of that ambiguity has become high enough that one participant is exiting the conversation rather than re-entering it.

A second, less certain hypothesis is that the avoidance is about the form of the conversations rather than the chores. If past talks ended in grievance or in one person doing most of the negotiating work, withdrawal is a sensible local strategy. I cannot tell from the material whether that is happening.

What I would try, roughly in order:

1. Separate the recurring disputes into the smallest repeated cases (e.g. kitchen surfaces, bins, bathroom, shared shopping). Do not start with a general talk about fairness; start with two or three concrete items that actually recur.

2. For each item, write down three things in a shared note: what counts as done, when it counts as done, and what happens when someone cannot do it. The third column matters because schedules change. "If you cannot do it by the agreed time, say so the day before and the other two decide" is different from "whoever notices does it."

3. Treat the written note as a draft, not a contract. Its purpose is to surface disagreement while it is still about a chore rather than about a person. If a written version feels too formal, a shared message thread or a note on the fridge does the same work with less ceremony.

4. Approach the friend who is avoiding the conversations separately and with a smaller ask. Not "we need to talk about the house," which invites the same argument, but "I noticed you've been quiet about this; I'd rather not keep pushing it in the group. Can we spend ten minutes on just the bins and the kitchen?" Give that person an easier entry point, and accept a lower-commitment role at first.

5. If the avoidance continues after one or two low-pressure attempts, stop treating it as a scheduling problem. Then the question becomes whether the living arrangement itself still works. That is a larger decision and should not be forced by a chore dispute, but it should not be indefinitely deferred either.

What I would avoid: a single big meeting intended to settle everything, moral language about "pulling weight," and counting instances as evidence in the moment. Those tend to convert a specification problem into a character dispute, which is exactly the shape the current disagreement already has.

I should be clear about what this is not. It is not a claim that the withdrawing friend is acting in good faith; I do not know. It is not a claim that the others are blameless. It is not a claim that written agreements work for every household. It is a conjecture that a large share of the recurring friction is ambiguity under shifting schedules, and that the ambiguity is addressable independently of who is right about any particular past disagreement. The strongest test of that conjecture is whether two or three concrete items, specified more tightly, stop recurring. If they do not, the hypothesis is wrong and the problem is probably about the relationship or the living arrangement rather than the chores.
COMMITMENTS
{"language":"FCL-1","records":[{"id":"c1","type":"claim","text":"A substantial part of the recurring chore friction is ambiguity in what spoken agreements specified, not disagreement about willingness to do chores.","scope":"This household, given the described pattern of later disagreement about what an agreement meant.","grounds":"The problem statement reports agreements that were later understood differently, plus changing schedules and one person avoiding the conversations."},{"id":"c2","type":"claim","text":"Treating each recurring chore as a small specification problem (done, by when, fallback if unable) is more likely to reduce recurrence than a general conversation about fairness or effort.","scope":"Ordinary shared-household chores.","consequence":"If two or three concrete items stop recurring after being specified more tightly, this supports c1; if they keep recurring, c1 is weakened and the problem is more likely relational or about the living arrangement."},{"id":"c3","type":"claim","text":"Approaching the avoiding flatmate one-to-one with a narrower ask is more likely to re-open the conversation than another group discussion.","grounds":"Avoidance is more plausibly about the form and stakes of the conversation than about any single chore; this is a conjecture, not an established fact."},{"id":"o1","type":"objection","text":"The account may be over-reading ambiguity. The avoidance could be about conflict fatigue, unequal load, or something outside the chores entirely, and formalizing chores could make things worse rather than better.","bearing":"If load imbalance or relational conflict is the real driver, the specification move in c2 may treat a symptom, and step 5 arrives too late."},{"id":"u1","type":"use","text":"Ask the reader to test c2 on two or three concrete recurring chores before adopting step 5, and to report whether recurrence falls.","action":"Read the account as a working hypothesis to try in the next week or two, not as an endorsed plan."},{"id":"p1","type":"problem","text":"The material does not say what the recurring chores are, how long this has gone on, or whether the withdrawing friend has said anything about why. Without that, all of the above stays at the level of a plausible but untested hypothesis.","mentions":["c1","c2","c3"]}],"uptake":["c1","c2","c3","o1","u1"]}

## Selected input objection

Source objection: daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/objection; selected view: both
Artifact: 406eff787391049a53c08a1fa638c1576c4a54c65be4bdde122593deb25fdbbe
Original body SHA256: 6dbebbfd0f40783c19873f2a045833055ecb090fecd9801cf39854f6f527ec0b
Original commitments SHA256: 9ffd96b23205ac092c5306bf372afa156fbb5159a3a259197c9ace200a835dc1
Delivery: COMPLETE; envelope: AUTHORED
BODY
I want to push on the account's central move: recasting the conflict as a problem of specification rather than a problem of motivation or fairness. That recasting is doing a great deal of work, and the material does not obviously support it.

Look at what the statement of the problem actually reports. Three people sharing a flat quarrel over routine chores. On occasion they agree who will do a task, and afterwards fall out over what the agreement meant. Timetables shift. One person has begun to steer clear of the conversations. The recurring "later disagreement about what it meant" is read by the account as evidence that the agreements were ambiguous. Yet the same observation is equally consistent with an alternative reading: the agreement was clear enough, and the later dispute is about whether the terms still bind given changed circumstances, or about who has standing to enforce them. "You said you'd do the bins" / "yes, and then my shift changed" is not necessarily a problem of semantics. It can be a problem of renegotiation, or one of legitimacy.

In o1 the account acknowledges this, yet it then treats the ambiguity hypothesis as the working one and gives less weight to the alternatives. That is a defensible starting point if one has to be chosen, but the diagnostic step the account itself proposes - try two or three concrete items and see if recurrence falls - is weaker than it looks, since a specification move can lower friction while the driver underneath is load imbalance or resentment. Tighter specs on a lopsided arrangement are still a lopsided arrangement, only with clearer paperwork. A fall in recurrence would be consistent with the ambiguity hypothesis, but the rival hypotheses forecast a different pattern: recurrence might fall on the items specified and resurface as fresh complaint items, or fall for a time and then come back at the next change of circumstances. These are not told apart by the account's test.

There is also an issue of phrasing worth flagging. The account states that the problem as posed is "practical" and the material is "thin." Those are the author's characterizations, not features of the situation. As a caution, calling the material thin is fine, but the thinness is then used by the account to license a good deal of construction (the three-column spec, the low-pressure approach to the withdrawing friend, the step-5 threshold). Thin material supports tentative proposals; it does not support ordering those proposals as if the ambiguity reading had already earned its place at the front.

Probably the most useful move in the account is the one it treats as secondary: that the avoidance may concern the form of the conversations rather than the chores. That deserves to be nearer the front, since it is the part of the situation that is genuinely distinctive and that the specific-negotiation advice does not address. A tight spec on bins does not bring a withdrawn flatmate back into the room. At c3 and step 4 the account half-sees this, yet the overall frame still centers the chores.

What I would not assert: that the ambiguity hypothesis is mistaken. I cannot judge from the material. My objection is to the ordering and to the strength of the test, not to the plausibility of the hypothesis. If the account were rewritten with the conversational-form reading as the first hypothesis and the spec move as one probe among several, I would have less to say against it.
COMMITMENTS

Load imbalance or resentment can sit alongside reduced friction on specified items, and recurrence may come back as fresh complaint items or after the following schedule change.","target":["p.objection.0#c2"],"bearing":"Weakens the claim that a fall in recurrence would confirm c1 and a rise in recurrence would refute it; the discriminating power of the test is lower than the account implies."},{"id":"o3","type":"objection","text":"The account describes the material as 'thin' and then licenses a fairly specific sequence (three-column spec, separate low-pressure approach, step-5 threshold for reconsidering the living arrangement). Thin material supports tentative probes; it does not support the presentation of that sequence as the natural order.","target":["p.objection.0#c2","p.objection.0#c3"],"bearing":"The order in which the account's recommendations are placed is doing prescriptive work that the stated evidence does not carry."},{"id":"c1","type":"claim","text":"The account's most distinctive observation - that avoidance may be about the form and stakes of the conversations rather than the chores - deserves to be closer to the front of the analysis, because the specific-negotiation advice does not address it.","scope":"This household, in view of the reported withdrawal from conversations.","grounds":"At c3 the account itself concedes this and at step 4 half-treats it, yet the overall frame still centers the chores."},{"id":"c2","type":"claim","text":"A lopsided or resented arrangement specified more tightly is still a lopsided or resented arrangement with clearer paperwork; specification alone does not address load imbalance or legitimacy.","scope":"Chore arrangements in shared households.","consequence":"A fall in recurrence on specified items is compatible with the ambiguity hypothesis and with the alternative hypotheses alike, so it should not be treated as confirmation of c1."},{"id":"o4","type":"objection","text":"My own objection may reach too far. If the flatmates genuinely cannot say what they agreed to, ambiguity is the plainest reading and the alternatives I am putting forward are harder to establish from the material than the account's reading is.","target":["o1","o2","c2"],"bearing":"If ambiguity is in fact the plainest reading, the objection comes down to a complaint about sequencing rather than about substance."},{"id":"p1","type":"problem","text":"Whether the later disagreements concern what the words meant, whether the agreement still binds after a schedule change, or who has standing to raise the issue is not stated by the material. These are distinguishable and the account does not tell them apart.","mentions":["o1","o2","c1"]},{"id":"u1","type":"use","text":"Ask for the account to be read with its own o1 taken as a live competitor rather than a caveat: set out the alternative readings (ambiguity, renegotiation, legitimacy) as rival hypotheses and build the probe to tell them apart, not merely to measure recurrence.","action":"Rework the framing so that the conversational-form reading and the ambiguity reading stand side by side, the spec move being one probe among several."}],"uptake":["o1","o2","o3","c1","c2","u1"]}

## Selected input rival

Source rival: daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/rival; selected view: both
Artifact: a6a817c086b877f919ae3a927d532ce46d007e49969962bcc613eb541fae0644
Original body SHA256: ca39bb97ac2b9415bd3d1cf52b318950797849095c017c0c99d3012020e45312
Original commitments SHA256: 5d08a79220b70ce3a31f83a3270998bbdd7ef386b3fb3297b5c883c067f05000
Delivery: COMPLETE; envelope: AUTHORED
BODY
The rival framing I want to try is not another chore protocol. It is the question of what the agreements were for.

The selected account treats the trouble as ambiguity in specifications: agreements lack criteria for done-ness and timing, schedules shift, so friction recurs. That is a good hypothesis as far as it goes, and I have no material that contradicts it. But it quietly assumes that everyone wanted a specification. The avoidance suggests the opposite for at least one flatmate. A person can stay away from a conversation not because the terms are vague but because any settled term would feel like a binding owed to people they live with, and that is a different problem from the one the selected account addresses.

So the rival pose is: maybe the disputes are not failing negotiations about tasks. Maybe they are negotiations about whether the flat is a unit with obligations or three private lives sharing fixtures. Under that reading, writing down "what counts as done" is not neutral — it is one side of a contested question, enacted without having settled it. Shifting schedules are then not merely a complication; they are the fact that makes the unit-reading feel coercive to the person who is withdrawing.

I cannot tell which reading is right from the material. What I can do is name a test that distinguishes them rather than assuming one. The selected account's test is whether tightened specifications stop recurrences. Mine adds a second: when specifications are proposed, does the withdrawing flatmate engage with their content or pull back from the proposal itself? Content-engagement supports the ambiguity reading. Pullback from the very idea of a written arrangement supports the unit-versus-privacy reading.

Roughly what I would do differently from the selected account:

1. Do not open with a shared note. Open by asking the two flatmates, separately, what they think the flat is — a shared project with mutual obligations, or three lives that happen to overlap in a kitchen. Do not ask it as a survey; ask it as a real disagreement I am willing to hear out.

2. If the answers diverge, treat that as the actual dispute, and treat the chores as the surface where it keeps surfacing. Chore rules can then be framed as a truce between two readings rather than as a correct specification that one side has been failing to meet.

3. Consider an arrangement that does not require agreement on meaning: individually-owned zones, or a rotation with a default outcome that nobody has to negotiate in the moment (for example, each person is responsible for a defined zone and the group does not audit it). This trades efficiency for reduced exposure, which is what a privacy-reading flatmate may actually want.

4. If one or both flatmates reject even truce-shaped arrangements, stop optimizing chores and start asking whether the lease and living arrangement still fit. That is not a chore failure.

What I am not claiming: that the withdrawing flatmate is the reasonable one, that written rules are coercive in general, or that the ambiguity reading is wrong. The selected account's diagnosis may well be correct and mine may simply add a second axis. The point of the rival is to make the second axis visible, because a plan that only addresses ambiguity will keep running into a wall if the disagreement is about what kind of household this is.
